title: Bound ragged encode staging to one kernel tile per shard
description: Split non-64-byte high/low transform encoding into a direct aligned prefix and a single staged 64-byte tail. Keep original staging and low parity scatter fixed at one tile per public shard rather than K/R full rounded shards, while preserving requested parity subsets and versioned wire bytes.

Candidate commit 97fe0ac (branch codex/leopard2-ragged-encode-tiling; based on decode scratch commits b7b0eb3 and 25bb6be) splits ragged transform encode into an aligned direct pass plus one staged 64-byte tail. title: Bound ragged decode staging to one kernel tile per coordinate

acceptance_criteria: Scratch queries demonstrate that increasing a ragged shard by complete 64-byte tiles grows only the selected N/side work term, not K+R staging; GF8 and even-byte GF16 tails at every boundary match aligned/materialized/direct oracles for generic/high/low, repeated and concurrent plans; no out-of-bounds reads/writes under guard pages and ASan/UBSan; TSan, strict, AArch64 compile, and isolated setup/execution/cache measurements pass without neighboring regression.

title: Bare active-LCH constants and derivative differential
description: Close the remaining correctness-foundation gap under Active-subspace LCH transform without conflating it with later production pruning. Add test-only hooks and independent direct algebra for bare active-length forward/inverse shifted-coset transforms, production FFTSkew/subspace normalization constants, low/high prepared locator factors, and normalized-basis derivative/output factors in GF8 and representative/all-power GF16 parents. Keep wire/profile behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Independent oracle compares production skew/normalization/prepared-factor tables and bare forward/inverse/derivative results for all legal GF8 dyadic lengths/aligned shifts plus representative/all-power GF16 active parents; scalar and available SIMD/backend outputs are identical; Release strict warnings, ASan+UBSan, and backend matrix pass; docs map every exposed factor to source/derivation; no production schedule claim is made; commit/evidence are recorded.
notes:
Read-only audit identified the bounded gap and one concrete UB hardening item. Current composed codec differential is strong but does not independently validate bare FFT/IFFT, FFTSkew/subspace normalizers, prepared low/high factors, or normalized-basis derivative/output factors. FF8/FF16 also form FFTSkew-1, a one-before-array pointer; replace with sentinel-backed or unbiased storage without changing logical indexing/wire bytes. Production branch-free pruning remains separately owned by 18.1.12/26. Note docs currently say generic dispatch remains until these gates, while specialized paths are already live, so factor evidence and wording must be reconciled.
Independent review after the first frozen checkpoint found no arithmetic, wire, sentinel-bound, derivative-direction, initialization, or ALTMAP defect. It did identify two test-only gaps before closure: GF16 inverse sizes >16 relied on production forward/inverse round-trip, and repeated symbols across ALTMAP lanes could hide lane pairing. Follow-up adds independent sparse large-parent values/inverse and lane-varying GF8/GF16 cases before final gates.
Final evidence commit 284c980. title: Make default worker pools affinity-aware and lazy
description: A focused backend/context audit found that default context creation uses std::thread::hardware_concurrency rather than the process allowed CPU set and eagerly starts thread_count-1 workers. On the current host, 32 online CPUs but 30 allowed CPUs yielded a reported default of 32 and 31 persistent pool workers, oversubscribing the affinity mask before any batch work. Detect the allowed CPU budget portably, cap deterministic defaults to it, and avoid instantiating worker threads until parallel execution actually needs them.
